items.text: The world and the markets are in a very different place from last February when Russia’s invasion of Ukraine started. Senior politicians and military leaders are debating the West’s further response to the war in Ukraine. The Security Conference in Munich, Germany, came days before the anniversary of Russia’s invasion, a conflict that reshaped commodity and energy flows and pushed up inflation and funding pressures globally. European stocks have risen in line with the recovery in business sentiment and activity, and the region may escape recession. The European Central Bank may decide to keep raising rates due to high inflation. Difficult international discussions over debt forgiveness get underway in India. Top of the agenda is the G20 Common Framework debt pact to allow the restructuring of low-income countries’ debts after the global health crisis. Difficult words: commodity (a substance or product that can be traded, bought, or sold), business sentiment (the overall health of the business environment), debt forgiveness (when a country or organization forgives a debt that doesn’t have to be paid back). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

These are some of the world’s most important business news of this week. One year ago, Russia invaded Ukraine, which changed the global business and energy market, and inflation rose in many countries. Politicians and military leaders met in Munich, Germany, to discuss further help to Ukraine. It seems that Europe may get out of recession because business activity is increasing. The European Central Bank is waiting for the latest data from stock markets . It will probably keep rising rates because inflation is very high. In 2020, G20 countries agreed to change the debt payments of the poorest countries. This week, 20 finance ministers met to discuss debt payments of middle-income countries and the possibility of forgiving debts after the pandemic. Difficult words: recession (a period of low business activity), stock market (a place where people or companies buy and sell parts of other companies), debt (money which someone owes and has to pay back). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

These are some of the most important business news. One year ago, the war in Ukraine starts. World business changes. Many countries start to have big problems. Everything gets more expensive. Politicians and military leaders meet in Munich, Germany. They speak about further help to Ukraine. It seems that the situation in Europe is getting better. Companies do more business. The European Central Bank will keep high rates because inflation is very high. 20 finance ministers meet in India. They speak about how to help poorer countries. These countries have debts. But they cannot pay them back. They start to have problems during the pandemic. Difficult words: military (connected to war and soldiers), rate (the amount in % which someone has to pay extra), inflation (the price of money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Fat Thursday is a Christian tradition in some countries. It is on the last Thursday before Lent, forty days of fasting before Easter. In Poland, people eat doughnuts on Fat Thursday. Polish doughnuts taste different because people fry them in oil for less than a minute. This way, the oil doesn’t get inside. Last Thursday, people waited in lines for hours to buy doughnuts. The prices of ingredients went up by almost 30% since last year, but it didn’t stop people from buying these special sweets. Until the 16 th century, doughnuts were not sweet. The dough was similar to bread, and there was pork fat inside. For frying, people usually used lard instead of oil. Difficult words: fast (not to eat or drink for some time), ingredient (one of the things which are in a meal), lard (a white substance from pig fat which people use for cooking). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Fat Thursday is a Christian tradition in some countries. It is on the last Thursday before Lent, forty days of fasting before Easter. In Poland, people eat doughnuts on Fat Thursday. Polish doughnuts taste different because people fry them in oil for less than a minute. This way, the oil doesn’t get inside. Last Thursday, people waited in lines for hours to buy doughnuts. The prices of ingredients went up by almost 30% since last year, but it didn’t stop people from buying these special sweets. Until the 16 th century, doughnuts were not sweet. The dough was similar to bread, and there was pork fat inside. For frying, people usually used lard instead of oil. Difficult words: fast (not to eat or drink for some time), ingredient (one of the things which are in a meal), lard (a white substance from pig fat which people use for cooking). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Fat Thursday is a tradition in some countries. It is on the last Thursday before Lent. Lent is a forty-day period of fasting before Easter. People in Poland make special doughnuts on Fat Thursday. These doughnuts are different from other doughnuts. People fry them in oil only for a short time. The oil does not get inside. The prices of ingredients go up by almost 30% since last year. It means that doughnuts are more expensive. But people still buy them. It is a tradition in Poland. In the past, doughnuts taste like bread. People put pork fat inside. In the 17 th century, people start making sweet doughnuts, too. Difficult words: fast (not to eat or drink for some time), ingredient (one of the things which are in a meal), tradition (something that people do for a long time without change). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Equatorial Guinea has confirmed its first outbreak of the Marburg virus, a highly infectious and deadly disease that’s similar to Ebola. Last week, the small Central African country quarantined more than 200 people and restricted movement in the Kie-Ntem province. In addition to nine deaths initially linked to a funeral ceremony in the province, the country has reported 16 suspected cases of Marburg virus with symptoms including fever, fatigue, blood-stained vomit, and diarrhea. Neighboring Cameroon also restricted movement along its border over concerns about contagion . According to the WHO, the virus can have a fatality rate of up to 88%, and there are no vaccines or antiviral treatments approved to treat it. Difficult words: contagion (the spreading of a disease by touching someone), fatality rate (the proportion of people who die from a disease among people diagnosed with it), antiviral (effective against viruses). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The WHO confirmed the first outbreak of the Marburg virus in Equatorial Guinea, a small country in Central Africa. Marburg virus is a highly infectious and very dangerous disease. It is similar to Ebola, and its symptoms include fever, tiredness, and diarrhea . According to the WHO, 88% of infected people die, and currently, there is no vaccine or medicine which stops the virus. Nine people died of the virus in the Kie-Ntem province, and more than 200 people were in quarantine . Cameroon, which neighbors Equatorial Guinea, watched the situation carefully and asked people not to travel to the country. Difficult words: infectious (a disease which spreads from person to person), diarrhea (when the body’s solid waste is more liquid than usual), quarantine (when someone has to stay away from others because he has or he may have a disease). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Marburg virus is a dangerous disease. It is similar to Ebola. Sick people have a fever and diarrhea . They are very tired, too. 88% of sick people die. The virus is very infectious. It means that it spreads from one person to another easily. Equatorial Guinea is a small country in Central Africa. Last week, the country confirms the outbreak of the Marburg virus. It happens in the Kie-Ntem province. Six people die. 16 people could have the virus. More than 200 people are in quarantine . They must not meet other people. At the moment, there is no medicine or vaccine for the virus. Difficult words: diarrhea (when the body’s solid waste is more liquid than usual), outbreak (when a disease suddenly starts somewhere), quarantine (when people who are sick or could be sick must not meet other people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Guanabara Bay is the backdrop to one of Rio de Janeiro’s most breathtaking views that enchanted countless visitors to Brazil, and it spans over 650 square kilometers. However, the bay is littered with abandoned sinking ships that leak toxic chemicals, and its waters are so filthy that most residents wouldn’t even consider swimming in them. But it’s not just the ships, raw sewage and garbage from the surrounding cities flow into the bay, too. This complicates fishing and poses a serious health hazard. Brazil’s Navy says that there are about 51 abandoned and capsized boats in the bay; however, the number’s likely higher. Ahead of the 2016 Rio Olympics, there were efforts to clean the bay, and millions of dollars were invested, but two years before the Games, Rio announced that it wasn’t going to meet its goal. Environmentalists have long called for the government to take action, but the pollution is getting worse. Difficult words: backdrop (everything behind that you’re looking at), enchant (to interest or attract someone very strongly), capsize (to turn over). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Guanabara Bay is in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, and it covers an area of more than 650 square meters. Many visitors love the view of the bay, but its waters are so dirty and dangerous that local people never swim in them. Sewage and garbage from several cities flow into the bay every day. Besides this, there are at least 51 abandoned ships, and toxic chemicals get into the water. Activists and fishermen asked the government to clean the bay, and before the 2016 Olympics, Rio promised to do it. International banks invested millions of dollars, but in the end, the government didn’t do anything, and the bay is getting dirtier every day. Difficult words: sewage (dirty water from houses and factories), garbage (things which people throw away), abandon (to leave behind). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Guanabara Bay is in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Many people visit it. They enjoy the beautiful view over the bay. There is a big problem. The waters in the bay are dirty and dangerous. Sewage and garbage from several big cities get into the bay. Another problem is that there are many abandoned ships. Officials say that there are at least 51 ships. Dangerous chemicals from the ships get into the water. Local people do not swim there. Fishermen cannot catch fish there anymore. The Olympics are in Rio in 2016. The government promises to clean the bay. Banks lend millions of dollars. But nothing happens. The bay is still dirty. Difficult words: sewage (dirty water from houses and factories), garbage (things which people throw away), abandon (to leave something or someone behind). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Three individuals aged 16, 17, and 20 entered a watch shop in Greater Santiago at midday, threatening staff and robbing several items. They went on to attack a woman and steal her car. Later, the woman anonymously told the local media that she did not want to give them her car and even kicked them twice. They punched her and she gave up when they showed her that they had a gun. The incident continued on the road with police chasing the stolen car. One police officer filmed as police surrounded the armed robbers. The police eventually managed to stop the vehicle and arrest the suspects , but only after one of them was shot. Difficult words: Greater (including nearby areas), chase (try to catch), armed (having a gun), suspect (=perpetrator – a person who did a crime). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Three individuals aged 16, 17, and 20 entered a watch shop in Santiago, Chile. They threatened the staff and robbed the shop. Then they attacked a woman and stole her car. She spoke to the media about the incident. At first, she did not want to give them the car. She even kicked them. One man hit her in the leg and another showed her a gun. When he showed her the gun, that was it. Police followed the car and managed to stop it. They surrounded it and arrested the men. The police shot one of them. Difficult words: threaten (if you threaten somebody, you make him or her do something by force), staff (the people who work somewhere), rob (to steal things from a place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from Santiago. Santiago is the capital of Chile. Three men go into a watch shop. They are 16, 17, and 20. They rob the shop. They leave the shop. They want to take a car. There is a woman in a car. She does not want to give it to them. She even kicks the men. One of the men hits her. Another man shows her a gun. She lets them have the car. The thieves drive away. The police go after them . The police stop the car. They arrest the thieves. The police shoot one of them. Difficult words: rob (to steal/take things from a place), a thief (a person who steals/takes things), to go after somebody (to try to catch somebody). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The European Parliament formally approved a law to effectively ban the sale of new gas and diesel cars in the EU from 2035. The move is part of the EU’s effort to speed up the switch to electric vehicles and combat climate change. The rules mean that car makers have to eliminate CO2 emissions from new cars sold by the middle of the next decade. The law will also set a 55% cut in CO2 emissions from new cars sold in 2030, compared to 2021 levels. That’s much higher than the current target of around 37%. EU countries agreed to the deal with lawmakers last October, and it’s expected that member states will make final approval in March this year. Many European car makers have invested heavily in electrification . For example, Volkswagen announced that it would only produce electric vehicles in Europe from 2033. Difficult words: combat (to fight), eliminate (to completely remove), electrification (replacing technologies and services that run on fossil fuels with ones that run on electricity). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Electrification is a process of replacing technologies and cars which run on gas or diesel with technologies that use electricity. In October last year, EU countries agreed that they would ban the sale of cars that run on gas or diesel. The European Parliament approved the law last week, and now, the governments must approve it, too. Everyone expects that they will do it in March this year. The law means that all cars sold from 2030 must have zero CO2 emissions . The cars sold from 2030 must produce 55% fewer CO2 emissions. European car makers are putting a lot of money into electrification. German carmaker Volkswagen said that it would only produce electric cars in Europe from 2033. Difficult words: replace (to put something in use instead of something else), approve (to officially agree with something), CO2 emission (gas which cars or factories produce when they burn coal, oil, or natural gas). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The EU wants to make only electric cars in the future. In October 2022, EU countries agree that they will sell only electric cars from 2035. It will not be possible to buy a car that runs on gas anymore. The European Parliament approves a law last week. This law bans the sale of other than electric cars from 2035. Cars, which car makers will sell from 2030, must have 55% fewer CO2 emissions . EU countries will probably approve the law in March this year. European car makers spend very much money on new technologies. Volkswagen is a German car maker. It will only produce electric cars in Europe from 2033. Difficult words: approve (to officially agree with something), ban (to officially stop something), CO2 emission (gas which cars and factories produce). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A network that listens for nuclear weapons detonations detected 26 major explosions on Earth between 2000 and 2013. Nuclear weapons caused none of them, but asteroid strikes caused all of them. California-based B612 Foundation released a visualization of what it would look like if a city-destroying asteroid hit the planet Earth. The chance of an asteroid striking our planet is in fact higher than scientists previously believed. There is already a NASA program in place that tracks asteroids larger than 1 kilometer. An object of this size would have global consequences if it struck the Earth. Difficult words: consequence (something that happens as a result of something else). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

An organization released a video. It shows an asteroid that hits Earth. The group uses the video to say that impacts of asteroids are common, more common than scientists believed. The video uses data from a global network. The network listens to nuclear weapons detonations . Between 2000 and 2013, 26 big explosions were detected . They were not caused by nuclear weapons but by asteroids. NASA watches asteroids that are larger than 1 kilometer. Difficult words: impact (the moment when one thing hits another), detonation (explosion), detect (to notice or discover). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An organization makes a video. It shows an asteroid. The asteroid hits Earth . The group says that asteroids hit Earth. There is a special system. It listens to big explosions . Between 2000 and 2013, 26 explosions were found. These explosions happened when an asteroid hit Earth. NASA watches big asteroids. These asteroids are bigger than 1 kilometer. Difficult words: organization (group of people who work on something), Earth (our planet), explosion (when something breaks quickly into small pieces). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Maple syrup is in higher demand than ever before; however, it comes at a time when rising temperatures are threatening the industry and pushing production farther north. It’s deep winter in Canada; however, it’s so warm on the northern fringe of the Quebec maple groves that tree sap has already started flowing. Such mild trends could boost Alan Bryson’s syrup-making operation, unlike with his southernmost US counterparts . Bryson’s yields have more than doubled in the past decade, and changing weather led to 2022 being his best year ever. US farmers are at the greatest risk. Data predicts that if temperatures don’t remain stable, maple sugaring areas could shrink . Milder temperatures mean that sap is less sweet and it takes more effort to produce maple syrup. Difficult words: sap (the fluid that circulates in a plant or tree), counterpart (another person or organization that has a similar function in a different place), shrink (to become smaller). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Quebec, Canada, is the world’s largest producer of maple syrup. Demand for maple syrup is higher than ever before, but changing weather brings new challenges . When temperatures are low, tree sap is sweet and it is easier to make maple syrup from it. But winters are getting milder and the sap starts flowing earlier than usual. Maple groves in Canada produce twice as much maple syrup as they did ten years ago, and it is great news for syrup-making companies. In the US, the situation is much worse. Warmer winters mean that there are fewer areas where it is possible to get tree sap. Difficult words: demand (when many people want to buy a product), challenge (a difficult task), sap (a liquid in a plant or tree). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Maple syrup is a sweet syrup from the sap of maples . Sap is a liquid in a plant or tree. Canada and the United States are the main producers of maple syrup. Quebec, Canada, is the largest producer of maple syrup in the world. In the past 10 years, Canada makes twice as much maple syrup as before. The reason is the weather. Winters are milder . Maples produce more sap. But when temperatures are low, the sap is sweeter. It is easier to make maple syrup from it. The situation is worse in the US. It is not possible to get sap in some areas. If the weather gets even warmer, some producers will stop their business. Difficult words: maple (a large tree that grows in northern areas of the world), liquid (a substance that flows), mild (not strong). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

European countries have spent nearly 850 billion dollars to fight soaring energy costs. A report by a Brussels-based think tank said that EU countries had allocated around 727 billion dollars in energy crisis spending, while Britain had allocated about 110 billion and Norway nearly 9 billion dollars. Germany spent the most, at 288 billion dollars. When Europe fell out with Russia last year, Russia cut off most of its gas deliveries to the continent, in retaliation for sanctions that the EU imposed on Russia due to the war in Ukraine. That sent gas costs soaring, and governments were forced to look for ways to protect consumers from enormous energy bills. According to the report, spending on the energy crisis was now similar to the EU’s Recovery Fund for the global health crisis that hit about 800 billion dollars. Europe tries to compete with subsidies in the United States and China, and countries are debating proposals to loosen state aid rules for green tech projects. Difficult words: think tank (a body of experts who provide advice and ideas on specific political or economic problems), retaliation (revenge), subsidy (payment by a government to a company as a form of help or assistance). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

When Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, the EU imposed sanctions on Russia. As a result, Russia stopped to deliver gas to Europe. This meant that prices of energy went up, and people were not able to pay their bills. Governments had to help these people and companies, too. A report by Brussels experts said that Europe already spent 850 billion dollars to solve the energy crisis. The EU allocated nearly 727 billion dollars, and Germany spent the most, 288 billion dollars. The report said that the EU’s costs on the energy crisis were now similar to spending on the coronavirus crisis, which was about 800 billion dollars. Difficult words: impose (to officially establish something), sanction (an action which a country takes to force another country to do something), allocate (to give something officially to someone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In February 2022, Russia starts a war with Ukraine. The EU wants Russia to stop the war. It introduces sanction s on Russia. Many companies stop doing business in Russia. Russia reacts to the sanctions. Russia doesn’t sell its gas to Europe anymore. It is a big problem for European countries. Prices of energy go up very much. People and companies don’t have enough money to pay their bills . Governments must help. Europe already spends 850 billion dollars on the energy crisis . Germany spends 288 billion dollars. It is the most in all of Europe. Difficult words: sanction (when one country takes action against another because the other country breaks a rule), bill (a piece of paper which says how much money someone must pay), energy crisis (a situation when there is not enough electricity or gas in a country or area). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The benefits of breastfeeding have been documented for years; however, it can be emotionally and physically overwhelming. According to the WHO, less than 50% of babies are breastfed for long enough. Some of the challenges stem from societal issues, for example, a lack of support, a lack of paid leave, or no lactation rooms at work. According to some experts, formula companies mislead people about the benefits of their products. They claim that the baby might sleep better, be calmer, or be more intelligent. A 2022 WHO report accuses companies of manipulating consumers and flooding the market. Formula companies also work through trusted sources like doctors. Doctors get incentives if they prescribe their products and companies pay for conferences or other social events. Some experts say that the support for parents has to change, so they have the opportunity to make informed decisions about how to feed their children. Difficult words: stem (to originate in), lactation room (a private space where a nursing mother can use a breast pump), incentive (a thing that motivates someone to do something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

When a baby is born, the mother can decide if she wants to breastfeed her child or use formula milk . Breastfeeding has many benefits, but it is not always easy. The WHO says that 50% of women don’t breastfeed for as long as their babies need. Many things make breastfeeding difficult, for example, no help in hospitals or no lactation rooms at work. Also, women often have to return to work, so they stop breastfeeding. The formula is an alternative to breastfeeding. But experts say that formula companies mislead women. Formula ads say that children, who drink formula, sleep better, are calmer, or are even more intelligent. Doctors get money from formula companies when they prescribe their products. According to experts, many women believe that formula is better than breastfeeding, and it must change. Difficult words: formula milk (a white powder that you mix with warm water and feed a baby with it), lactation room (a place where a mother can pump milk out of her breasts), mislead (to make someone believe something that is not true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

When a woman has a baby she can breastfeed the baby or she can use formula. Breastfeeding means that the baby drinks the woman’s milk. It is very healthy for the child. The problem is that 50% of women don’t breastfeed long enough. Sometimes they don’t get any help. Sometimes they must go back to work. Women can buy formula. The formula is a powder . You mix it with warm water. The baby drinks it instead of the mother’s milk. Formula companies want to make money. Many formula ads are on TV and social media. These ads say that children who drink formula sleep better. They are calmer and more intelligent. Many parents believe it. But it is not true. Difficult words: breastfeed (to feed a baby with milk from the breast), powder (a dry thing that has small pieces), ad (a short film that makes people want to buy a product or service). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Qatar said that it will donate 10,000 mobile homes to quake-hit areas in Turkey and Syria. The cabins were originally used to house soccer fans during the 2022 World Cup. The first batch of container houses should soon arrive in Turkey, and it will provide comfortable accommodations to earthquake victims. Each unit has a classy interior, two beds, and necessary furniture. The accommodations, cabins, or caravans, were always planned to be donated as part of the World Cup legacy plans. In November 2022, Qatar already pledged to donate 6,000 cabins that were used in fan villages to the homeless in Kenya. Difficult words: batch (a group of things of the same kind), classy (attractive or of excellent quality), pledge (to promise). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Qatar promised to send 10,000 mobile homes to Turkey and Syria. Soccer fans used these homes during the 2022 World Cup. Each cabin has 16 square meters, and there are two beds and furniture. Qatar will send the cabins to people who lost their homes after last week’s earthquakes. Qatar always planned to donate the homes, but after the disaster in Turkey, the plans changed. The first batch of mobile homes already left Qatar, and they will arrive in Turkey soon. In November 2022, Qatar promised to give 6,000 mobile homes to homeless people in Kenya. Difficult words: mobile home (a building in which people live and which can be moved to another place), donate (to give money or things to people who need them), batch (a group of similar things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

During the 2022 Soccer World Cup in Qatar, fans and athletes live in mobile homes . Qatar plans to donate these homes to people who need them. In November 2022, Qatar says that it will 6,000 mobile homes to people in Kenya. Now, Qatar helps Turkey and Syria. The earthquake is in Turkey and Syria last week. Thousands of people are without a home. Qatar will send 10,000 mobile homes to Turkey and Syria. Some mobile houses are already on the way to Turkey. Each home has 16 square meters. It has two beds and furniture . Difficult words: mobile home (a home which can people move to another place), donate (to give money or things to people who need them), furniture (a table, chair, desk, and similar things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

One of the most accomplished composers of the 20 th century, Burt Bacharach, died at 94. Bacharach achieved a string of top 10 hits from the 1950s to the 21 st century. His songs included ‘Walk On By’, ‘I Say A Little Prayer’, and ‘Do You Know The Way To San Jose’. He was a three-time Oscar winner, receiving two Academy Awards in 1970 for the score of ‘Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid’ and ‘Raindrops Keep Fallin’ On My Head’. Bacharach wrote material for Aretha Franklin, Dusty Springfield, and Tom Jones, and his songs were covered by many artists. In 2012, Barack Obama presented him with the Gershwin Prize. According to his publicist, Bacharach died last week on Wednesday at his Los Angeles home of natural causes. He is survived by his fourth wife Jane Hansen, their children Oliver and Raleigh, and his son Christopher. Difficult words: accomplished (highly skilled), covered (performed in a new version). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

US composer Burt Bacharach died at the age of 94. Bacharach was one of the greatest songwriters ever. He won an Oscar three times. In 1970, he won two Oscars for music for ‘Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid’ and ‘Raindrops Keep Fallin’ On My Head’. Bacharach wrote music for many famous singers, including Aretha Franklin and Dusty Springfield. Many artists covered his songs, the most famous of which were ‘Walk On By’ or ‘I Say A Little Prayer’. Bacharach was married four times and he had four children. He died in his home in Los Angeles. Difficult words: composer (a person who writes music), cover (to make a new version of an old song). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Burt Bacharach is a US songwriter . He writes music. Bacharach is one of the best songwriters ever. He wins three Oscars. One Oscar is for the music for ‘Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid’. Bacharach writes music for many famous singers. For example Aretha Franklin or Dusty Springfield. His biggest hits are ‘Walk On By’ and ‘I Say A Little Prayer’. Many artists cover his songs. Bacharach is married four times. He has four children. Last week, he dies in his home in Los Angeles. He is 94 years old. Difficult words: songwriter (a person who writes songs and music), cover (to make a new version of an old song). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A drone footage was captured after several earthquakes shook Turkey and Syria last week. According to Italian seismologists , a series of powerful earthquakes that struck Turkey have likely moved the entire country by up to six meters. Two major earthquakes of magnitudes 7.8 and 7.5 killed over 22,000 people, and rescuers have still been searching through the rubble for more bodies. The footage was taken from the Kahramanmaras province, the epicenter of the earthquake. Satellite images showed how the ground had been deformed along and near the East Anatolian fault line. In lots of places, the lines of rupture went right through buildings. The rupture of the first earthquake was around 300 kilometers long, and the second big event ruptured another 140 kilometers. To put those distances in context, London to Paris is roughly 345 kilometers. Difficult words: seismologist (an expert in the study of earthquakes), epicenter (the part of the earth’s surface directly above the origin of an earthquake), deform (to change the shape or structure). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A series of strong earthquakes hit Turkey and Syria last week. More than 22,000 people died, but many bodies were still under the rubble . The first earthquake had a magnitude 7.8 and it caused a crack more than 300 kilometers long. The second strong earthquake had a magnitude 7.5 and it cracked another 140 kilometers. This crack is called a fault line, and it moved Turkey by almost six meters. In many places, the fault line goes directly through houses and roads. A drone footage showed the front line in the Kahramanmaras province, where was the epicenter of the earthquake. The front line completely changed the land and towns. Difficult words: rubble (pieces of walls or buildings), magnitude (a number which says how strong and earthquake is), epicenter (a place above the center of an earthquake). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Several strong earthquakes hit Turkey and Syria last week. The strongest two earthquakes have a magnitude 7.8 and 7.5. The ground cracks . The crack is called a fault line. The fault line in Turkey is more than 440 kilometers long. In some places, it is up to 6 meters wide. The whole country moves. The fault line goes through hills, fields and towns, too. It destroys roads, bridges and buildings. More than 22,000 people die in the earthquakes. Rescuers are still looking for many people. Thousands of people are in the rubble . Difficult words: magnitude (how strong an earthquake is), crack (when something breaks and it makes a line on the surface of something), rubble (pieces of houses and walls). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A group of 35 countries, including the United States, Germany, and Australia, will demand that Russian and Belarusian athletes are banned from the 2024 Olympics in Paris, France. Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskiy took part in the online meeting attended by 35 ministers to discuss the call for the ban, and he pointed out that 228 Ukrainian athletes and coaches died as a result of the Russian invasion. Ukraine has threatened to boycott the games if Russian and Belarusian athletes compete, and Ukrainian boxer Oleksandr Usyk said that Russians would win medals of blood, deaths, and tears if they were allowed to take part. However, according to officials, it wasn’t time to talk about a boycott yet, because most participants of the meeting, except for Greece, France, and Japan, were in favor of an absolute exclusion of Russian and Belarusian athletes. Almost 18 months before the Olympics are due to start, the International Olympic Committee is desperate to calm the waters and not jeopardize the Games’ message of global peace, and it suggests that Russian and Belarusian athletes could compete as neutrals. Difficult words: boycott (to refuse to buy a product or take part in an activity as a way of expressing strong disapproval), calm the waters (to restore peace or calm a person or situation), jeopardize (to put at risk). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

35 ministers took part in an online meeting to discuss a ban on Russian and Belarusian athletes to take part in the 2024 Olympics in Paris, France. Almost all ministers agreed with the ban, but Greece, France, and Japan were against it. Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskiy said that 228 Ukrainian athletes and coaches already died in the war with Russia. Ukraine said that it would boycott the Olympics if Russian and Belarusian athletes competed . The International Olympic Committee hopes that it will not be necessary for Ukraine to boycott the Games. The IOC suggests that Russian and Belarusian athletes could compete as neutrals . Difficult words: boycott (not to take part in something or to buy a product as a way of protest), compete (to take part in a game or match), neutral (an athlete who competes at an international event but he doesn’t represent his country). Famous letters are on auction; they were written by Princess Diana during her divorce proceedings with Prince Charles. Diana sent the letters to her friends Tarek and Susie Kassem between 1995 and 1997, and many of the letters explained the pressure she felt and her hope that 1997 would be an easier year. The Kassems are selling the collection in 32 individual slots through Lay’s Auctioneers in Penzance, Cornwall, UK. The auction expects to sell the letters for more than 100,000 dollars, and they will donate the proceeds to charities that Diana supported. Difficult words: proceeding (a formal event or action), slot (an item sold at an auction), proceeds (money from an event or activity). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Between 1995 and 1997, Princess Diana wrote 32 letters to her friends Terek and Susie Kassem. Now, the Kassems are selling the letters in auction . Diana wrote the letters during the time that she divorced Prince Charles. She wrote about how difficult this time was for her, and she hoped that 1997 would be a better year. She also wrote that if she knew how difficult the divorce would be, she would never have agreed to go it. Auctioneers expect to sell the letters for more than 100,000 dollars. The Kassems will give the money to charities which Diana supported. Difficult words: auction (a place where people sell things and one person buys things if they offer the most money), auctioneer (a person who is in charge of an auction), charity (an organization which gives food or money to people who need it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On a normal Singapore street sits a normal house, but it does not contain a normal collection. This house has one of the largest private collections of Barbie dolls in the world at 6,000 dolls. Jian Yang is the proud owner of all of these dolls and even calls some of them “ precious “. One of his favourites is Great Shape Barbie that was from 1984 and was featured in the movie “Toy Story”. He paid up to $3,600 for one of his dolls, making this an expensive hobby. Jian’s obsession predictably affects his relationships. He says that some ex-girlfriends felt insecure because they could not look like one of the dolls, which are infamous for their unrealistic waistlines . Difficult words: precious (important and valuable), feature (something that is an important part), obsession (too strong an interest in something), insecure (not feeling good), infamous (famous for something that people do not like), waistline (the size of one’s waist). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A man from Singapore has a large collection of Barbie dolls . It is one of the biggest collections in the world. The man owns 6,000 Barbie dolls. His most precious Barbie is his first Barbie. He bought it back in 1984. This type of Barbie was also in a popular movie called “Toy Story”. The hobby of collecting Barbies can be an expensive one. His most expensive doll cost him $3,600. The man’s hobby of collecting Barbies doesn’t have a good effect on his relationships . No girl can be as perfect as a Barbie. Difficult words: doll (a toy that looks like a small person), precious (very important), relationship (feelings between two people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

According to economists, Brexit costs 120 billion dollars a year in lost output , with the effects to business investment and to the ability of companies to hire workers. Brexit hit the economy faster than many experts expected. A report suggests that Britain’s GDP is 4% smaller than if it had stayed in the EU. Business investments are 19% less than the G7 average, and experts blame Brexit uncertainty for the change. The report also estimates the EU has 370,000 fewer workers than before Brexit, and this figure is only partially offset by the arrival of non-EU citizens. For many people, Brexit was always more than simple numbers and the precise cost isn’t easy to know with the Ukrainian crisis and the pandemic. However, Britain has a long way to make Brexit successful and to close the gap with its major peers. Difficult words: output (production), GDP (the production of goods and services in a country during a certain time), offset (to balance). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Experts predicted that Brexit would have a negative impact on Britain’s economy, but nobody thought that the impact would already happen. A report says that after Brexit, Britain loses 120 billion dollars every year, and the impacts are visible in all areas of business. The report says that Britain’s GDP is 4% smaller than if Britain stayed in the EU. Around 370,000 EU workers left the country, and the worst situation is in the transport and storage sectors . The government is trying to solve the problem by hiring workers from outside the EU, but the attempt is not helping the situation very much. People cannot really say how much exactly Brexit costs because of the pandemic and war in Ukraine. They brought new challenges for Britain and the EU. Britain will have major difficulty to return to the levels it had before Brexit. Difficult words: GDP (all the things and money that a country makes during a certain time), sector (an area of business), challenge (a difficult task). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The pandemic and war in Ukraine make bigger problems for the country. Difficult words: sector (area of business), hire (to give someone a job), goods (things which companies sell). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Miracle Mineral Solution, or MMS, has been around since the 1990s. The chemical is one part sodium chloride, a chemical disinfectant , and one part acid. MMS is industrial grade bleach that smells like a very chlorinated swimming pool. The chemical shot in popularity in 2020 after former US president Donald Trump suggested disinfectant as a possible COVID treatment. If you drink MMS, it can kill you; however, this fact didn’t stop tens of thousands of people around the world from using it to cure all kinds of conditions, including Autism, COVID-19, and arthritis. According to toxicologists, MMS kills bacteria and germs, and it kills human tissue, too. A survey showed that 6% of respondents reported they inhaled bleach vapors , and 4% reported they drank or gargle d it. In 2020, federal officials arrested some of the biggest sellers of MMS, but consumer bleach is still for sale on mainstream shopping sites like Amazon and eBay. Difficult words: disinfectant (a chemical liquid that destroys bacteria), gargle (to hold and rinse a liquid in the mouth or throat), vapor (a substance in the form of gas that mixes with the air). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 2020, former US president Donald Trump said that disinfectant may help treat COVID-19. MMS is an industrial bleach which went on sale in the 1990s. It kills bacteria and germs, and it will kill parts of a person who drinks it. Although experts warn that MMS cannot be drunk, thousands of people inhale d or drank it. They believed that it can cure many situations, from Autism, to COVID-19, or arthritis. In 2020, officials arrested some sellers of MMS, but people can still buy it on many sites, such as Amazon and eBay. Difficult words: disinfectant (a chemical which destroys bacteria), bleach (a chemical which people use to make materials whiter, for example to clean sinks, swimming pools, and so on), inhale (to breathe in gas, smoke, or air). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: inhale (to breathe in air, gas, or smoke), cure (to make healthy again), arthritis (an illness which causes pain in some body parts). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

For the fifth year in a row, the Danish capital Copenhagen was full of beautiful light installations as the 23-day Copenhagen Light Festival took over the city. From February 3 until February 26, 2023, the harbor and city space will be lit with illuminated bridges, buildings, and light art, all scattered around the city. You can see light on dark drifting clouds, beautiful old buildings, architectural squares, and the city’s canals. Visitors can experience the installations by themselves or join one of the festival’s guided tours by Segway , canal boat, kayak, or guided walk. Difficult words: scattered (spread out all over a place), drift (to move slowly and continuously from one place to another), Segway (an electric vehicle with two wheels and a base between them on which the rider stands). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Light illuminates bridges, old buildings, squares, and the city’s canals. Visitors can enjoy 35 installations all over the city. People have many ways to explore the festival. Visitors can take a guided tour by Segway , canal boat, kayak, a guided walk, or a walk by themselves. Difficult words: installation (an art structure), illuminate (to shine a light on something), Segway (a vehicle with two wheels and a bottom on which the rider stands). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Early Monday morning, a powerful 7.8 magnitude earthquake hit parts of Turkey and Syria. According to the US Geological Survey, the earthquake struck near the town of Gaziantep, Turkey, and it was 10 kilometers deep. The earthquake toppled hundreds of buildings and killed thousands of people. According to officials, thousands of children may be among the dead following the earthquake and aftershocks . Hundreds are still believed to be trapped under rubble, and the death toll is expected to rise. Local people and rescue workers spent the night searching for survivors in metal tangles and giant concrete piles. Countries around the world are sending support to help the rescue efforts, including specialist teams, sniffer dogs and equipment. However, the earthquake caused significant damage to three airports across Turkey which created challenges for aid deliveries. Turkey is near several fault lines and is one of the world’s most active earthquake zones. Difficult words: aftershock (a smaller earthquake that follows a large one), sniffer dog (a dog trained to find things or people by smell), fault line (a long crack in the surface of the earth). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On early Monday morning, a strong earthquake hit Turkey and Syria. The earthquake had a magnitude of 7.8 and it was 10 kilometers deep. Hundreds of buildings collapsed and thousands of people were trapped in the rubble . The first reports said that at least 12 000 people died in Turkey and 3 500 died in Syria, but authorities expected the number to grow. Local people and rescue workers searched the rubble all night to pull out many people, including children. Many countries are sending help to Turkey, but the earthquake damaged three airports in the country, so people cannot easily deliver things to the affected areas. Difficult words: magnitude (a number which says the strength of an earthquake), trapped (be in one place and unable to move), rubble (broken pieces of buildings). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
